public_rationale: The speaker hedged this as his reading of the evidence. The record bears out each factual point he lists. TechCrunch reported in October 2023 that Rabbit is a rebranding of Cyber Manufacture Co., the company behind the GAMA NFT project. A former GAMA engineer told Protos that GAMA was put on hold when the team's priority shifted. Rabbit's December 2023 release put its total funding at $30 million. Engadget reported that Rabbit was selling the $199 R1, with batches selling out and shipping in spring 2024. Rabbit disputes that GAMA was abandoned and says it was completed and open-sourced. That bears only on his characterization 'disappearing on its users', which his hedge covers. It does not undercut the same-entity, gadget, or $30 million points.
limitations: The claim is hedged. It is graded as the speaker's reading of the record, not as a certain statement.
'Disappearing on its users' is a contested characterization and was not scored strictly.

our_interpretation: 'From what I can tell' marks this as the speaker's reading of the evidence, not a claim of certainty. The test is whether the public record bears out the factual points he lists. A hedged reading confirmed by the record counts as supported. It is not held to a stricter standard than he set.
'Exact same corporate entity' means the company that ran GAMA (Cyber Manufacture Co.) and the company selling the R1 (Rabbit Inc.) are one renamed entity.
'Selling an AI-powered gadget' is met by Rabbit selling and shipping the R1 by early May 2024.
'$30 million in venture capital' means Rabbit's announced cumulative funding as of the post. Funding is not revenue.

'Disappearing on its users' is the speaker's description of GAMA going dormant. It is covered by his hedge and checked only loosely: did GAMA activity stop or get shelved within months before the R1 went on sale?
criteria.support_condition: The record shows Cyber Manufacture Co., GAMA's company, became Rabbit Inc. It also shows GAMA was an NFT project that was later shelved, Rabbit was selling the R1 by spring 2024, and Rabbit had announced $30 million in total funding.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The record shows the NFT seller and the R1 seller are different legal entities, or Rabbit's announced funding before the post was materially different from $30 million, or Rabbit was not selling the R1 by May 2024.
